Here’s a 12-week strength program structured into three progressive phases. Goal: build full-body strength with emphasis on the big lifts, while maintaining movement quality and resilience. Frequency: 4 days/week. Each session includes a primary lift, a secondary strength movement, accessories, and brief conditioning or core. Progression uses RPE and %1RM ranges to auto-regulate while driving overload.

Global notes
- Warm-up each day: 5–8 min easy cardio + joint prep (hips/shoulders/ankles) + 2–3 ramp-up sets for the main lift.
- Tempo: default controlled eccentric (~2–3s) unless noted.
- Rest: main lifts 2–4 min, accessories 60–90s.
- RPE guidance: RPE 7 = ~3 reps in reserve (RIR); RPE 8 = ~2 RIR; RPE 9 = ~1 RIR.
- Load progressions: when all sets at the target RPE feel easier (e.g., RPE 7 feels like RPE 6), add 2.5–5 kg next week for that lift.
- Conditioning: optional 10–15 min Zone 2 (bike/row) post-workout 2x/week if recovery allows.
- Deloads are built in Week 4 and Week 8.
- Testing/realization in Week 12.

Weekly split
- Day 1: Lower A (Squat emphasis)
- Day 2: Upper A (Bench emphasis)
- Day 3: Lower B (Deadlift emphasis)
- Day 4: Upper B (Overhead/bench accessory emphasis)

Phase 1: Foundation and Volume (Weeks 1–4)
Focus: refine technique, build work capacity, accumulate volume at moderate loads.

Week 1
- Day 1 (Lower A)
  - Back Squat: 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8 @ RPE 7
  - Split Squat (DB): 3x10/side
  - Leg Curl (seated/lying): 3x12
  - Plank: 3x45–60s
- Day 2 (Upper A)
  - Bench Press: 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - Bent-Over Row (barbell): 4x8 @ RPE 7
  - DB Incline Press: 3x10
  - Lat Pulldown or Pull-Up: 4x6–8 (assisted as needed)
  - Face Pull: 3x12–15
  - Side Plank: 3x30–45s/side
- Day 3 (Lower B)
  - Conventional Deadlift: 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Front Squat: 3x6 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust (barbell): 3x10
  - Reverse Lunge: 3x8/side
  - Calf Raise: 3x12–15
- Day 4 (Upper B)
  - Overhead Press (barbell): 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Chest-Supported Row: 4x8
  - Close-Grip Bench Press: 3x8
  - Single-Arm DB Row: 3x10/side
  - DB Lateral Raise: 3x12–15
  - Hanging Knee Raise: 3x10–12

Week 2
- Increase load slightly (2.5–5 kg on barbell lifts) while holding rep schemes.
- Keep RPE 7–8 on main lifts.
- Same exercise menu as Week 1.

Week 3
- Slight bump in volume or intensity:
  - Back Squat 5x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Bench Press 5x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Deadlift 5x4 @ RPE 7–8
  - OHP 5x4 @ RPE 7–8
- Accessories unchanged.

Week 4 (Deload/Technique)
- Reduce volume ~40–50% and intensity to RPE 6.
  - Back Squat 3x4
  - Bench Press 3x4
  - Deadlift 3x3
  - OHP 3x3
- Accessories: 2 sets each, lighter, clean technique.
- Optional extra mobility, no failure work.

Phase 2: Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)
Focus: heavier loading, moderate volume, introduce doubles/triples and pause/tempo to drive strength.

Week 5
- Day 1 (Lower A)
  - Back Squat: 5x4 @ RPE 8
  - Paused Squat (2-sec pause): 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - RDL: 3x6–8
  - Leg Press: 3x8–10
  - Ab Wheel or TRX Fallout: 3x8–12
- Day 2 (Upper A)
  - Bench Press: 5x4 @ RPE 8
  - 2-Count Paused Bench: 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - Pendlay Row: 4x6
  - DB Incline Press: 3x8
  - Face Pull: 3x12–15
  - Copenhagen Plank: 3x20–30s/side
- Day 3 (Lower B)
  - Deadlift: 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - Deficit Deadlift (1–2"): 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - Front Squat: 3x4–6 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust: 3x8
  - Calf Raise: 3x12–15
- Day 4 (Upper B)
  - Overhead Press: 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - Close-Grip Bench: 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Chest-Supported Row: 4x6–8
  - Pull-Ups or Assisted: 4x4–6
  - Lateral Raise: 3x12–15
  - Hanging Leg Raise: 3x8–10

Week 6
- Slight load increase across main lifts if Week 5 was ≤RPE target.
- Keep same rep schemes as Week 5.
- Swap an accessory variation if desired (e.g., cable row for chest-supported row).

Week 7
- Intensify:
  - Back Squat 6x3 @ RPE 8
  - Bench Press 6x3 @ RPE 8
  - Deadlift 6x2 @ RPE 8
  - OHP 6x2 @ RPE 8
- Pause variations: 3x2–3 @ RPE 7 after primary lifts (lighter than Week 5).
- Accessories reduced to 2–3 sets each to prioritize recovery.

Week 8 (Deload/Speed)
- Back Squat: 4x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6), focus bar speed.
- Bench Press: 4x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- Deadlift: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- OHP: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- Minimal accessories: 2x10 light, mobility, breathing drills.

Phase 3: Peak Strength and Realization (Weeks 9–12)
Focus: low-to-moderate volume, high intensity; refine singles; test in Week 12.

Week 9
- Day 1 (Lower A)
  - Back Squat: work to 1@RPE 8 (top single), then 3x3 @ 85% of that single
  - Pause Squat: 2x2 @ RPE 7
  - RDL: 3x5–6
  - Core: Cable Pallof Press 3x10/side
- Day 2 (Upper A)
  - Bench Press: 1@RPE 8, then 4x3 @ 82–85% of that single
  - 2-Count Paused Bench: 2x2 @ RPE 7
  - Row (any): 4x6–8
  - Rear Delt Fly: 3x12–15
- Day 3 (Lower B)
  - Deadlift: 1@RPE 8, then 3x2–3 @ 85% of that single
  - Front Squat: 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6–8
  - Calf Raise: 3x10–12
- Day 4 (Upper B)
  - Overhead Press: 1@RPE 8, then 4x2–3 @ 82–85%
  - Close-Grip Bench: 3x4–5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Pull-Ups: 4xAMRAP leaving 1–2 reps in tank
  - Lateral Raise: 3x12–15
  - Hollow Body Hold: 3x30–45s

Week 10
- Similar to Week 9 with a small progression:
  - Aim for 1@RPE 8–8.5 on main lifts, add 1–2% load if bar speed/technique holds.
  - Back-off work: 3–4 sets of 2–3 reps at 85–88% of the day’s top single.
  - Keep accessories minimal (2–3 sets).

Week 11 (Taper into heavy practice)
- Day 1: Back Squat 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~85%
- Day 2: Bench Press 1@RPE 9; then 3x2 @ ~85%
- Day 3: Deadlift 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Day 4: OHP 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Accessories: very light, 1–2 sets of 8–12 for balance; prioritize sleep and mobility.

Week 12 (Test/Realize)
- Day 1: Test Back Squat — warm-up to singles; attempt new 1RM based on Week 11. Then 2x3 @ ~80% to groove pattern.
- Day 2: Test Bench Press — same structure.
- Day 3: Test Deadlift — same structure.
- Day 4: Optional pressing/accessory flush: 3x8 light pump work, mobility, walking. If fatigued, rest.

Progression and loading guide
- If no established 1RMs, estimate after Week 3 using e1RM from best set (e.g., reps and load with RPE).
- Typical weekly jumps:
  - Squat/Deadlift: 2.5–5 kg
  - Bench/OHP: 1–2.5 kg
- Technique rules: stop sets if form degrades (butt wink, knee cave, bar path issues). Keep 1–2 RIR on accessories.

Accessory rotations (optional swaps to manage fatigue or equipment)
- Rows: chest-supported, cable, single-arm, seal row.
- Pulldown variations: neutral, wide, single-arm.
- Single-leg: Bulgarian split squat, step-up, reverse lunge.
- Hamstrings: RDL, leg curl, Nordic eccentrics (2–3x5).
- Push accessories: DB incline, dips (assisted), machine press.
- Shoulders: lateral raise, Y-raise, rear delt cable fly.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night, consistent schedule.
- Daily steps: 6–10k for general recovery.
- Mobility: 5–10 min post-lift focusing on tight areas (hips, T-spine, lats/pecs).
- Deload adherence is non-negotiable; reduce other life stress where possible in Weeks 4, 8, 12.

Simple nutrition guidance for strength
- Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day across 3–5 meals.
- Calories: slight surplus (+150–300 kcal/day) if body comp allows to support strength; maintain if preferring recomposition.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day; prioritize 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein 1–2 h pre-training and similar post.
- Hydration: 2–3+ L water/day; add electrolytes if sessions are long/sweaty.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, daily.

Example day structure
- Warm-up: 5 min bike + dynamic hips/shoulders.
- Main lift ramp: 5–8 reps empty bar, 5 @ 40%, 3 @ 60%, 2 @ 70%, then work sets.
- Post-lift: accessories, core, optional 10 min Zone 2.
- Cooldown: breathing (2–3 min), light mobility.

This plan gives a clear week-by-week progression, built-in deloads, and a test week to realize strength gains while managing fatigue. Adjust loads using RPE and the client’s day-to-day readiness.

To ramp hinge volume sensibly, use a simple, trackable framework that controls three knobs—exposure (sessions/week), volume (hard sets/reps), and intensity (RPE/load/ROM)—and only turns one knob at a time. Here’s a practical scheme you can run from Week 7 onward with clear guardrails and decision rules.

1) Define the hinge “dose” you’re tracking
- Count only working hinge sets at RPE ≥5: RDLs, block pulls, tempo hinges, hip thrusts. Exclude warm-ups and drill-only PVC hinges.
- Track per-week:
  - Total hinge hard sets
  - Total hinge volume load (sets x reps x load) for RDLs/hip thrusts
  - Highest hinge RPE hit and longest ROM used

2) Weekly progression template (Weeks 7–12)
- Exposure: 2 hinge exposures/week (e.g., RDL day + block pull day). Keep at 2 until Week 10–11.
- Intensity caps:
  - Week 7: RPE ≤6
  - Week 8: RPE ≤6 (deload feel—maintain or add 1 rep per set only)
  - Week 9: RPE ≤7
  - Week 10: RPE ≤7 on RDLs; block pulls ≤7, optional floor technique singles ≤6 if cleared
  - Week 11: RPE ≤7–8 on RDLs; technique singles ≤7
  - Week 12: RPE ≤7 across the board (consolidate)
- Volume targets (hard hinge sets/week, not counting squats/leg press)
  - Week 7: 5–6 total sets (e.g., RDL 3x6 + block pull 2–3x3)
  - Week 8: 5–6 sets (same load; you may add +1 rep/set or +1 light set if recovery excellent)
  - Week 9: 6–8 sets (e.g., RDL 4x6 + block pull 3–4x3)
  - Week 10: 7–9 sets (e.g., RDL 4x6–8 + block pull or 4x2–3; or replace 1 block-pull set with 2–4 x 1 floor singles @ RPE 6)
  - Week 11: 8–9 sets max (cap here to avoid overreach), with RDL at slightly higher effort (RPE 7–8)
  - Week 12: 6–8 sets (taper volume 15–25% from Week 11, keep quality)
- ROM progression rules
  - Progress ROM before load: mid-shin → just below knee → mid-shin from floor setup → floor (technique singles only).
  - Change only one: if you deepen ROM this week, keep load and reps steady.

3) Set-rep prescriptions you can plug in
- RDL day
  - Week 7: 3x6 @ RPE 5–6, ROM to just below knee
  - Week 8: 3x6–7 same load or +1 rep/set, same ROM
  - Week 9: 4x6 @ RPE 6–7, ROM to mid-shin
  - Week 10: 4x6–8 @ RPE 7, ROM to mid-shin or just above ankle if perfect
  - Week 11: 3–4x5–6 @ RPE 7–8, same ROM
  - Week 12: 3x6 @ RPE 6–7, −5–10% load from Week 11
- Block pull/technique pull day
  - Week 7: Blocks set just below knee, 3x3 @ RPE 5–6, 2–3 s controlled eccentric
  - Week 8: Same load/ROM, 3x3 smoother; optional +1 set if zero symptoms
  - Week 9: Lower blocks to mid-shin, 3–4x3 @ RPE 6–7, 1-s pause below knee on first rep
  - Week 10: Keep mid-shin 4x2–3 @ RPE 6–7 OR 4–6 x 1 from floor @ RPE 6 if cleared
  - Week 11: 5–6 x 1 technique singles @ RPE 6–7 from floor OR 4x2–3 @ RPE 7 from mid-shin
  - Week 12: 3–4 x 2 @ RPE 6–7 from best-tolerated height; 1–2 technique singles @ RPE ~7 if appropriate

4) Decision checkpoints each session
- During: any pulling discomfort >2–3/10, hamstring grab, or asymmetrical shifting? Stop the set, regress ROM and/or load immediately.
- 24-hour check: if next-morning tightness/soreness >3/10 or lasts >48 h, reduce next week’s hinge volume by 25–40% (sets first), keep RPE cap.
- Performance cue: bar speed stays snappy; if rep velocity drops >20% mid-set, terminate the set to stay within RPE cap.

5) How to progress load sanely
- Use 2–5% load bumps when all sets hit target RPE and no symptom flare for 48 h.
- If you deepen ROM, hold load steady; only increase load the following week if still symptom-free.
- RDLs: straps allowed to keep form; prioritize neutral spine and constant hamstring tension without stretch pain.

6) Balance with the rest of the week
- Keep squats/leg press at RPE 6–7 while hinge ramps.
- Separate the two hinge exposures by at least 48 h.
- Keep conditioning all Zone 2 on a bike/elliptical until Week 10; only add short fast spins if zero symptoms.

7) Simple tracking sheet (columns to log)
- Exercise; ROM/height; Sets x Reps; Load; Top-set RPE; Notes on symptoms during/after/next day.
- Weekly totals: hinge hard sets; RDL tonnage; highest RPE; ROM status (tick box).

- Day 3: Deadlift 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Day 4: OHP 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Accessories: very light, 1–2 sets, RPE 5–6; prioritize sleep/mobility

- Sequence: If deadlift is priority, test it first this week; otherwise squat → bench → deadlift
- Test days (for each main lift)
  - Warm up to strong singles; attempt new 1RM or performance PR guided by Week 11
  - Then 2x3 @ ~80% to groove pattern, optional
- Day 4: Optional light pump (3x8 easy) and mobility only; or rest if fatigued

- Session 1: Zone 2 25–35 min (bike/erg/incline walk)
- Session 2: Short repeats with low fatigue

- Exposure: 2 hinge exposures/week throughout (RDL/variation + DL/variation)
- Weekly hinge hard set targets

  - W5: 8–10; W6: 9–10; W7: 8–9; W8 (deload): 4–5
  - W9: 6–8; W10: 6–8; W11: 4–6; W12: 3–5

Accessory rotation menu (swap as needed to manage fatigue/equipment)
- Hamstrings: RDL/DB RDL, leg curl (seated > lying), Nordic eccentrics (2–3x4–5 in Weeks 1–6)

- Upper back: chest-supported row, Pendlay row, single-arm row, seal row, face pulls, rear delt fly
- Quads: front squat, leg press, heel-elevated squats, split squats/step-ups
- Grip: farmer carries, bar holds, towel hangs (use straps on high-rep hinges to preserve grip for DL day)

- Sleep 7.5–9 h; daily steps 6–10k
- Mobility 5–10 min post-lift (hips, T-spine, lats/pecs)
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs 3–5 g/kg/day (front-load on DL day)
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; 20–30 g protein + 30–60 g carbs 1–2 h pre- and post-training
- Hydration 2–3+ L/day; electrolytes for longer/sweaty sessions

Example weekly layout
- Mon: Lower A
- Tue: Upper A
- Wed: Conditioning Session 1 (Zone 2, 30–40 min)
- Thu: Lower B
- Fri: Upper B
- Sat: Conditioning Session 2 (per phase, 25–40 min)
- Sun: Off, light walk/mobility

This unified plan restores full training with a posterior-chain/deadlift emphasis, integrates sensible hinge volume ramps, and respects recovery via planned deloads and conditioning placement so she can peak cleanly in Week 12.

Here’s the consolidated 12-week program with all adjustments integrated: posterior-chain emphasis for deadlift strength, two weekly conditioning sessions, and the sensible hinge ramp that bridges rehab back to full training. It’s written assuming we restart at Week 1 now that she’s cleared. If you’re resuming mid-block, start at the applicable week.

Frequency and split
- 4 lifting days/week
  - Day 1: Lower A (Squat + Hamstrings/Glutes)
  - Day 2: Upper A (Bench + Heavy Row)
  - Day 3: Lower B (Deadlift Focus)
  - Day 4: Upper B (Overhead + Pull Emphasis)
- 2 conditioning sessions/week
- Warm-up each day: 5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic hips/T-spine/shoulders + ramp-up sets
- Tempo: controlled eccentrics (~2–3 s) unless noted; pause work as prescribed
- Rest: main lifts 2–4 min, accessories 60–90 s
- RPE anchors: main lifts RPE 7–9 across phases; accessories 1–2 RIR
- Progression: add 1–2% or 2.5–5 kg on lower lifts and 1–2.5 kg on presses when all sets land ≤ target RPE with solid speed

Conditioning overview (2x/week, hinge-friendly)
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Zone 2 + 60/60 intervals with carries
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Tempo/threshold + power intervals/sled; deload Week 8 to Zone 2 only
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Maintain with low-impact Zone 2 + very short repeats; taper near testing
- Place conditioning away from heavy lower days when possible (e.g., Wed/Sat)

Posterior-chain emphasis principles
- Hinge exposures 2–3x/week (main DL + RDL/variations)
- Rotate pauses/deficits/blocks for off-floor strength; maintain hamstring work (RDL, curls) and upper-back density (rows/pulls)
- Use straps on RDL/hip thrusts to save grip for heavy deadlifts; include specific grip holds separately

Phase 1: Foundation and Volume (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: technical refinement, build work capacity, add posterior-chain volume. Week 4 deload.

Week 1
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back Squat: 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Romanian Deadlift: 4x8 @ RPE 7
  - DB Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8/side
  - Leg Curl (seated/lying): 4x10–12
  - 45° Back Extension: 3x12, glute squeeze
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench Press: 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - Chest-Supported Row (heavy): 5x6–8 @ RPE 7–8
  - DB Incline Press: 3x10
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral): 4x8
  - Face Pull: 3x12–15
  - Farmer Carry: 4x20–30 m heavy
- Day 3 Lower B (Deadlift focus)
  - Conventional Deadlift: 5x4 @ RPE 7
  - Pause Deadlift (1–2 s mid-shin): 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust: 4x8
  - Reverse Lunge or Step-Up: 3x8/side
  - Standing Calf Raise: 3x12–15
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Overhead Press: 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Pendlay Row: 4x6–8 @ RPE 7–8
  - Close-Grip Bench: 3x8
  - Single-Arm Cable Row: 3x10/side
  - Hanging Knee Raise: 3x10–12

Week 2
- Progress loads slightly if RPE allows; repeat structures
- Option: add one set to leg curl or back extension if recovery is good

Week 3
- Small intensity bump with hinge priority
  - Deadlift 6x3 @ RPE 7–8
  - RDL 4x6–7 @ RPE 7–8
  - Back Squat 5x4 @ RPE 7–8
  - Rows remain heavy: 4–5x6–8
- Keep hip thrust 4x8; other accessories unchanged

Week 4 (Deload/technique)
- Reduce volume ~50% and intensity to RPE 6
  - Deadlift 3x3; Squat 3x3; RDL 2x6 light; OHP/Bench 3x3–4 @ RPE 6
- Accessories: 2 sets each, light and crisp
- Conditioning reduced (see below)

Conditioning Weeks 1–4
- Session 1: Zone 2 steady-state 30–40 min (bike/row/jog/incline walk)
- Session 2: 6–8 x 60 s moderate-hard (RPE 7) / 60 s easy on bike/rower + 6–8 min carry circuit (farmer/suitcase)
- Week-by-week
  - W1: 30 min Z2; 6 x 60/60 + 6 min carries
  - W2: 32–35 min Z2; 7 x 60/60 + 7 min carries
  - W3: 35–40 min Z2; 8 x 60/60 + 8 min carries
  - W4 (deload): 25–30 min Z2; replace intervals with 10–12 min easy tempo, no carries

Phase 2: Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: heavier loading, improve off-floor strength, maintain hamstrings/upper back. Week 8 deload.

Week 5
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back Squat: 5x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - RDL: 4x6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Leg Curl: 4x8–10
  - 45° Back Extension (hold plate): 3x10–12
  - Ab Wheel/TRX Fallout: 3x8–12
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench Press: 5x4 @ RPE 8
  - Pendlay Row (from floor): 5x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Weighted or Assisted Pull-Up: 4x5–6
  - Face Pull: 3x12–15
  - Grip: Bar hold in rack 3x20–30 s @ ~70–80% DL work-set weight
- Day 3 Lower B (Deadlift focus)
  - Deadlift: 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - Deficit Deadlift (1–2"): 3x3 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust: 4x6–8 heavy
  - Front Squat: 3x4–6 @ RPE 7
  - Calf Raise: 3x12–15
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Overhead Press: 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - Close-Grip Bench: 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Chest-Supported Row or Cable Row: 4x6–8
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral): 3x8–10
  - Hanging Leg Raise: 3x8–10

Week 6
- Slight load increase if Week 5 was on-target
- Keep two hamstring moves on each lower day; accessories can rotate

Week 7
- Intensify while prioritizing hinges
  - Deadlift 6x2 @ RPE 8
  - Pause Deadlift 3x2 @ RPE 7 after main DL
  - Back Squat 4x3 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 3x5 @ RPE 8
- Upper back: rows 4x5–6 heavy; pull-ups 4xAMRAP leaving 1–2 RIR
- Trim accessories to 2 sets each to manage fatigue

Week 8 (Deload/Speed)
- Back Squat: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6), bar speed focus
- Bench: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- Deadlift: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- OHP: 3x2 @ ~70% (RPE 6)
- Minimal accessories: 2x10 light; mobility/breathing

Conditioning Weeks 5–8
- Session 1: Tempo/threshold aerobic
  - 10 min easy → 20 min “comfortably hard” (RPE 6–7) → 5 min easy
- Session 2: Power intervals + sled
  - Bike/erg: 10 x 45 s hard (RPE 8–9) / 75 s easy
  - Finisher: 8–10 x 20 m sled push, walk-back
- Week-by-week
  - W5: Full volumes as above
  - W6: Same or +1 interval / +2 min tempo
  - W7: Keep volume, aim higher quality
  - W8 (deload): Z2 only 25–30 min; skip intervals/sled

Phase 3: Peak Strength and Realization (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: practice heavy singles, maintain hamstring and upper-back support with minimal fatigue; test squat/bench/dead in Week 12.

Week 9
- Day 1 Lower A
  - Back Squat: work to 1@RPE 8; 3x3 @ 82–85%
  - RDL: 3x5–6 @ RPE 7–8
  - Leg Curl: 3x8–10
  - Pallof Press: 3x10/side
- Day 2 Upper A
  - Bench Press: 1@RPE 8; 4x3 @ 82–85%
  - Heavy Row (barbell or chest-supported): 4x5–6
  - Rear Delt Fly: 3x12–15
  - Grip: Bar hang 3x max quality or 3x20–30 s towel hangs
- Day 3 Lower B (Deadlift practice)
  - Deadlift: 1@RPE 8; 3x2–3 @ 85% of the day’s single
  - Pause Deadlift: 2x2 @ RPE 7
  - Hip Thrust: 3x5–6 heavy
  - Calf Raise: 3x10–12
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Overhead Press: 1@RPE 8; 4x2–3 @ 82–85%
  - Close-Grip Bench: 3x4–5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Pull-Ups: 4xAMRAP leaving 1–2 RIR
  - Lateral Raise: 3x12–15
  - Hollow Body Hold: 3x30–45 s

Week 10
- Repeat Week 9 structure; aim for 1–2% load bump if bar speed/technique hold (RPE 8–8.5 on singles)
- Back-off work: 3–4 sets of 2–3 reps at 85–88% of the day’s single
- Keep hamstring accessories at 2–3 sets to support without excess fatigue

Week 11 (Taper/realization practice)
- Day 1: Back Squat 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~85%
- Day 2: Bench Press 1@RPE 9; then 3x2 @ ~85%
- Day 3: Deadlift 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Day 4: OHP 1@RPE 8.5–9; then 2x2 @ ~82–85%
- Accessories: very light, 1–2 sets, RPE 5–6; prioritize sleep/mobility

Week 12 (Test/Realize)
- Sequence: If deadlift is priority, test it first this week; otherwise squat → bench → deadlift
- Test days (for each main lift)
  - Warm up to strong singles; attempt new 1RM or performance PR guided by Week 11
  - Then 2x3 @ ~80% to groove pattern, optional
- Day 4: Optional light pump (3x8 easy) and mobility only; or rest if fatigued

Conditioning Weeks 9–12
- Session 1: Zone 2 25–35 min (bike/erg/incline walk)
- Session 2: Short repeats with low fatigue
  - Bike/erg: 8 x 20 s fast (RPE 8) / 100 s easy
  - Weeks 11–12: cut volume in half and avoid intervals within 48 h of testing

Hinge volume ramp and guardrails (baked in)
- Exposure: 2 hinge exposures/week throughout (RDL/variation + DL/variation)
- Weekly hinge hard set targets
  - W1: 7–8; W2: 7–9; W3: 8–10; W4 (deload): 4–5
  - W5: 8–10; W6: 9–10; W7: 8–9; W8 (deload): 4–5
  - W9: 6–8; W10: 6–8; W11: 4–6; W12: 3–5
- Only progress one variable/week (load, reps, or ROM). If any posterior-chain tightness >3/10 lingers >48 h, trim next week’s hinge sets by 25–40% and hold load.

Accessory rotation menu (swap as needed to manage fatigue/equipment)
- Hamstrings: RDL/DB RDL, leg curl (seated > lying), Nordic eccentrics (2–3x4–5 in Weeks 1–6)
- Glutes/hip extension: hip thrust, barbell glute bridge, 45° back extension, cable pull-through
- Upper back: chest-supported row, Pendlay row, single-arm row, seal row, face pulls, rear delt fly
- Quads: front squat, leg press, heel-elevated squats, split squats/step-ups
- Grip: farmer carries, bar holds, towel hangs (use straps on high-rep hinges to preserve grip for DL day)

Recovery and nutrition
- Sleep 7.5–9 h; daily steps 6–10k
- Mobility 5–10 min post-lift (hips, T-spine, lats/pecs)
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; carbs 3–5 g/kg/day (front-load on DL day)
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; 20–30 g protein + 30–60 g carbs 1–2 h pre- and post-training
- Hydration 2–3+ L/day; electrolytes for longer/sweaty sessions

Example weekly layout
- Mon: Lower A
- Tue: Upper A
- Wed: Conditioning Session 1 (Zone 2, 30–40 min)
- Thu: Lower B
- Fri: Upper B
- Sat: Conditioning Session 2 (per phase, 25–40 min)
- Sun: Off, light walk/mobility

This unified plan restores full training with a posterior-chain/deadlift emphasis, integrates sensible hinge volume ramps, and respects recovery via planned deloads and conditioning placement so she can peak cleanly in Week 12.
